title: Apple restricts dating apps and AI companions to users 18 and up
content:
Apple is adjusting its App Store policies to make it more difficult for minors to use online dating apps or AI companions that engage in “sexual or romantic content,” the tech giant shared in an announcement to developers on Monday.
The new rules follow other changes the company has made to better protect minors, which include the rollout of its age assurance technology globally and more parental controls and child safety features.
While most major dating services typically restrict their platform to adults, Apple’s new policy will require all apps offering dating or romantic relationship features to carry an 18+ rating. Starting November 16, developers will be required to include new content descriptors to ensure their app’s age ratings reflect its features, the company said.
It’s perhaps more interesting how this rule could impact AI companion apps, or those where such functionality is one of many features. Often targeted at younger people, Character.AI, Replika, and other AI apps let people create AI companions, including friends, lovers, boyfriends and girlfriends, and other fantasy characters.
xAI last year also launched 3D animated AI companions that allowed users to unlock NSFW capabilities. As of last summer, top AI companion apps across the Apple App Store and Google Play had been downloaded 220 million times globally.
In addition to “dating and relationships,” apps will also need to indicate if they are sharing the real-world locations of a user with another person or group as part of their functionality. Any app doing so raises obvious privacy concerns, especially if the user wasn’t aware that their location was being shared.
The company noted that in Brazil, apps that provide location-sharing features for families can request an official rating from the government’s Ministry of Justice and Public Security (MJSP/Ministério da Justiça e Segurança Pública), instead of being required to list them with the A16 rating, as the local law requires.

report.summary: Apple will force dating apps and AI companion apps with romantic or sexual features to carry an 18+ App Store rating starting November 16.
report.background: Apple has spent the past two years tightening child-safety rules across its platforms, rolling out age-assurance technology globally and expanding parental controls. The App Store's age-rating system had grown outdated as app categories blurred: a chatbot that offers friendship, roleplay or romance looked identical on paper to a homework helper. Regulators added pressure too, with laws in the US, UK and Brazil demanding stricter age verification and clearer disclosures about how apps handle minors' data. Meanwhile the AI companion market exploded, with apps like Character.AI, Replika and xAI's animated companions drawing hundreds of millions of downloads, often skewing young. Apple's answer is to shift responsibility onto developers: declare what your app actually does, and the rating follows automatically.
key_points: Starting November 16, developers must attach new content descriptors to their App Store listings, so ratings reflect real in-app features rather than self-selected categories. Any app offering dating or romantic-relationship functionality will be bumped to an 18+ rating, whether or not dating is its main purpose.

AI companion apps are the sleeper target. Products like Character.AI, Replika and xAI's animated companions let users build virtual boyfriends, girlfriends and fantasy characters; if romantic or sexual content is involved, they now fall under the adult-only bucket.

Apple is also forcing disclosure of real-world location sharing. Apps that pass a user's location to another person or group must say so in their listing, a privacy move aimed at features minors may not understand they've enabled.
The rules follow Apple's global age-assurance rollout and expanded parental controls, extending a broader child-safety push from hardware and accounts into the App Store's metadata layer.
Brazil gets a carve-out: family location-sharing apps can request an official rating from the Ministry of Justice and Public Security instead of the A16 rating local law would otherwise require.
report.impact: For the AI industry, this is the first major platform-level classification of AI companionship as adult content, and it lands on a category with 220 million-plus downloads. Expect developers to either strip romantic and sexual features to keep teen audiences, or segment products into teen-safe and 18+ versions with separate listings. Smaller companion startups face real revenue risk, since App Store ratings drive discovery and gate downloads. Developers broadly get a compliance chore: auditing features, rewriting store metadata and documenting content policies before mid-November. For users, minors lose easy access to romantic AI chatbots and dating apps, while adults face more friction and age checks. The location-sharing disclosure arguably matters most day to day, giving everyone clearer warning when an app broadcasts where they are.
report.tools: Watch how major companion apps respond: Character.AI, Replika and xAI's Grok companions will reveal the compliance playbook. To track the rules, bookmark Apple's App Store Review Guidelines page on age ratings and its developer news updates. For parents, Apple's Screen Time and Communication Limits settings are the practical follow-up. Researchers wanting download and rating data can use Sensor Tower or Appfigures for App Store trend tracking.
